faqs.question: What is a healthy BMI?
faqs.answer: A healthy BMI for adults is typically between 18.5 and 24.9.

faqs.question: How accurate is BMI?
faqs.answer: BMI is a useful screening tool but can be misleading for athletes or elderly individuals.

faqs.question: How often should I check my BMI?
faqs.answer: Monthly checks are sufficient for most adults.

faqs.question: Does BMI differ for men and women?
faqs.answer: The calculation is the same, but women typically have more body fat at the same BMI.

faqs.question: How do I calculate BMI for children?
faqs.answer: Children's BMI uses age and sex-specific growth charts as percentiles.

faqs.question: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
faqs.answer: Eat 500 fewer calories than your TDEE for about 1 pound loss per week.

faqs.question: What's the minimum calories I should eat?
faqs.answer: Women: at least 1200. Men: at least 1500 calories.

faqs.question: How accurate are calorie calculators?
faqs.answer: They provide estimates. Track intake for 2-3 weeks to find your true needs.

faqs.question: Should I eat back exercise calories?
faqs.answer: Generally, eat back about half of exercise calories.

faqs.question: Do calories matter more than macros?
faqs.answer: For weight change, total calories are most important. For body composition, macros matter too.

faqs.question: What is TDEE?
faqs.answer: Total Daily Energy Expenditure - the total calories you burn in a day including all activities.

faqs.question: How is TDEE different from BMR?
faqs.answer: BMR is calories at rest. TDEE includes BMR plus activity calories.

faqs.question: Which activity level should I choose?
faqs.answer: Be honest - most people overestimate. Sedentary if desk job, lightly active if exercise 1-3x/week.

faqs.question: How do I use TDEE for weight loss?
faqs.answer: Eat 500 below TDEE to lose ~1 lb/week.

faqs.question: Should I recalculate TDEE as I lose weight?
faqs.answer: Yes, recalculate every 10-15 lbs lost.

health/bmr.introText: BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) is the number of calories your body burns at complete rest. It's the foundation for calculating your total daily calorie needs.

faqs.question: What is BMR?
faqs.answer: Basal Metabolic Rate - calories burned at complete rest for basic body functions.

faqs.question: Why is BMR important?
faqs.answer: BMR accounts for 60-75% of daily calories. It's the base for calculating calorie needs.

faqs.question: Can I increase my BMR?
faqs.answer: Yes - building muscle increases BMR. Each pound of muscle burns ~6 calories/day at rest.

faqs.question: Which BMR formula is most accurate?
faqs.answer: Mifflin-St Jeor is considered most accurate for most people.

faqs.question: Is BMR the same as RMR?
faqs.answer: Similar but RMR (Resting Metabolic Rate) is slightly higher as it includes minimal activity.

faqs.question: What are macros?
faqs.answer: Macronutrients: protein, carbohydrates, and fat. They provide calories and serve different body functions.

faqs.question: How much protein do I need?
faqs.answer: 0.7-1g per pound of bodyweight for most active people. More if building muscle.

faqs.question: What macro ratio is best for weight loss?
faqs.answer: Higher protein (30-40%), moderate carbs (30-40%), moderate fat (20-30%) works for most.

faqs.question: Do I need to track macros?
faqs.answer: Not required, but helpful for optimizing body composition and performance.

faqs.question: What's the difference between macros and calories?
faqs.answer: Calories measure energy. Macros are the nutrients that provide those calories.

faqs.question: What is a healthy body fat percentage?
faqs.answer: Men: 10-20% is healthy, 6-13% is athletic. Women: 18-28% is healthy, 14-20% is athletic.

faqs.question: How accurate is this calculator?
faqs.answer: The Navy method is within 3-4% of more precise methods like DEXA scans.

faqs.question: Is body fat percentage better than BMI?
faqs.answer: Yes, body fat percentage distinguishes between muscle and fat mass, unlike BMI.

faqs.question: How do I measure my waist correctly?
faqs.answer: Measure at the narrowest point, usually at the navel level. Relax and don't suck in.

faqs.question: How often should I check body fat?
faqs.answer: Monthly is sufficient. Body fat changes slowly.

faqs.question: How is ideal weight calculated?
faqs.answer: Multiple formulas use height as the base, adjusted for gender. We show results from 4 methods.

faqs.question: Why do different formulas give different results?
faqs.answer: Each formula was developed for different populations. The range between them is your healthy zone.

faqs.question: Does frame size matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, people with larger bone structures can be healthy at higher weights.

faqs.question: Is ideal weight the same as goal weight?
faqs.answer: Ideal weight is a healthy range. Goal weight is personal and may differ based on your preferences.

faqs.question: Should I aim for the lowest ideal weight?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The middle of your healthy range is often most sustainable.

faqs.question: How much protein do I need daily?
faqs.answer: 0.8g per kg minimum. For muscle building, aim for 1.6-2.2g per kg of bodyweight.

faqs.question: Can I eat too much protein?
faqs.answer: For healthy individuals, up to 2g/kg is safe. Excess protein is used for energy or excreted.

faqs.question: When should I eat protein?
faqs.answer: Spread intake across 3-5 meals. Post-workout protein is beneficial but not required immediately.

faqs.question: Is protein powder necessary?
faqs.answer: No, but it's a convenient way to meet protein targets if you can't get enough from food.

faqs.question: Does protein help weight loss?
faqs.answer: Yes, protein increases satiety and preserves muscle during calorie deficit.

health/ovulation.metaTitle: Ovulation Calculator - Find Your Fertile Days | CalcMaster
health/ovulation.metaDescription: Free ovulation calculator predicts your most fertile days. Track your cycle, find your ovulation date, and increase chances of conception.
health/ovulation.introText: Ovulation typically occurs 14 days before your next period. Our calculator predicts your fertile window to help with family planning or conception.
health/ovulation.formula: Ovulation Day = Last Period Start + Cycle Length - 14 days

faqs.question: When do I ovulate?
faqs.answer: Typically 14 days before your next period. For a 28-day cycle, around day 14.

faqs.question: What is the fertile window?
faqs.answer: The 5 days before ovulation plus ovulation day - when pregnancy is possible.

faqs.question: How accurate is this calculator?
faqs.answer: Good estimate for regular cycles. For irregular cycles, consider ovulation tests.

faqs.question: Can I get pregnant outside the fertile window?
faqs.answer: Very unlikely. Sperm survives 5 days, egg survives 12-24 hours.

faqs.question: What are signs of ovulation?
faqs.answer: Cervical mucus changes, slight temperature rise, mild cramping (mittelschmerz).

health/due-date.introText: Pregnancy typically lasts 40 weeks from the first day of your last menstrual period. Our calculator estimates your due date and shows your pregnancy timeline.

benefits.title: Multiple Methods
benefits.description: Calculate by LMP, conception, or ultrasound

faqs.question: How is due date calculated?
faqs.answer: Add 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of your last menstrual period.

faqs.question: How accurate is the due date?
faqs.answer: Only 5% of babies arrive on their due date. Most arrive within 2 weeks before or after.

faqs.question: What if I don't know my last period?
faqs.answer: An ultrasound can estimate due date based on baby's measurements.

faqs.question: When does each trimester start?
faqs.answer: 1st: weeks 1-12. 2nd: weeks 13-26. 3rd: weeks 27-40.

faqs.question: Can my due date change?
faqs.answer: Yes, ultrasound measurements may adjust the due date, especially in early pregnancy.

faqs.question: How do I count pregnancy weeks?
faqs.answer: Pregnancy is counted from the first day of your last menstrual period, not conception.

faqs.question: Why am I 4 weeks pregnant if I conceived 2 weeks ago?
faqs.answer: Pregnancy counting includes the 2 weeks before conception when dating from LMP.

faqs.question: How big is my baby at X weeks?
faqs.answer: Our calculator shows size comparisons for each week (poppy seed at 4 weeks, blueberry at 8 weeks, etc).

faqs.question: When should I see a doctor?
faqs.answer: First prenatal visit is typically at 8-10 weeks. Call earlier if you have concerns.

faqs.question: Is pregnancy 9 or 10 months?
faqs.answer: It's about 9 calendar months or 10 lunar months (40 weeks).

health/sleep.name: Sleep
health/sleep.metaTitle: Sleep Calculator - Find Your Optimal Bedtime | CalcMaster
health/sleep.metaDescription: Free sleep calculator finds your optimal bedtime or wake time based on sleep cycles. Wake up feeling refreshed by timing your sleep right.
health/sleep.heroSubtitle: Find your optimal sleep and wake times
health/sleep.introText: Sleep cycles last about 90 minutes. Waking up between cycles helps you feel more refreshed. Our calculator finds the best times to sleep and wake.
health/sleep.formula: Optimal Sleep = Wake Time - (90 min × Number of Cycles) - 15 min to fall asleep

faqs.question: How many hours of sleep do I need?
faqs.answer: Most adults need 7-9 hours. That's 5-6 complete sleep cycles.

faqs.question: What is a sleep cycle?
faqs.answer: A 90-minute pattern of light sleep, deep sleep, and REM. You go through 4-6 per night.

faqs.question: Why does waking between cycles matter?
faqs.answer: Waking during deep sleep causes grogginess. Between cycles, you wake more easily and feel refreshed.

faqs.question: Why is 15 minutes added?
faqs.answer: Average time to fall asleep. Adjust if you fall asleep faster or slower.

faqs.question: Is it better to get less sleep or wake mid-cycle?
faqs.answer: Often better to sleep one less cycle than wake during deep sleep.
